name: Central Nervous System Organization and Anatomical Axes

reference.source: Clinical Neuroanatomy Made Ridiculously Simple / Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy
clinicalPearls: Cephalic flexure induces a ninety-degree bend between brainstem and diencephalon, shifting anatomical axes
Prosencephalon subdivides into telencephalon (cerebrum) and diencephalon (thalamus, hypothalamus)
Rhombencephalon subdivides into metencephalon (pons, cerebellum) and myelencephalon (medulla oblongata)
Dura mater forms falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli, separating supratentorial and infratentorial spaces
Epidural hematoma is biconvex from middle meningeal artery rupture; subdural hematoma is crescentic from bridging vein shear
reference.pathophysiology: Structural development of the neural tube establishes five secondary brain vesicles surrounding ventricular cavities. Disruptions in neural tube closure cause anencephaly rostrally and spina bifida caudally. Mechanical acceleration-deceleration forces produce traumatic shearing of bridging veins or middle meningeal artery lacerations within specific meningeal compartments.
additionalInvestigations: Non-contrast head CT for acute intracranial hemorrhage
MRI brain T1, T2 and FLAIR for parenchymal architecture
CT venography for dural venous sinus thrombosis
